# SEV-1 INCIDENT - RELEASE BLOCKER
**Title:** Statements are filing some payments under the wrong kind of transaction, or dropping the payee name
**Owner:** Payments Operations
**Disposition:** Do not ship this release until it is resolved

## What customers reported

Over the past few days support has collected a run of tickets that all share one
shape: the money itself moved fine, but the app files the payment under a category
that does not match what the customer actually did, or shows the wrong name - or
no name at all - beside it. In every case the row that misbehaves carries one very
particular, uncommon form of raw statement text; everyday rows are labeled exactly
as before. The tickets below are anonymized, but the raw narration each customer
pasted is reproduced verbatim, because that raw text is what makes each case
reproducible.

> "I wrote a cheque against my account and the app just lists it as a general
> transfer now - nothing marks it as a cheque anymore. My earlier cheques were
> tagged correctly. The only thing sitting in that row's note is the cheque's own
> number, nothing else around it."

> "My salary came in and the amount is right, but where my employer's name should
> be the app now just prints the word `NACH`. The raw text on that row looks like
> `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` - it used to lift the employer's name off the end
> of that reference, and now it is picking up the wrong piece of it."

> "On some transfers that come in, the sender's name is blank now. Those rows all
> share the same reference layout - a short block of letters, then a long string
> of digits, then the name - for example `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`. The name
> sitting at the end just is not being pulled through anymore; the name column
> comes out empty."

The same batch of complaints also covers two quieter cases that are about the
category rather than the name. The token confirmation charge a bank posts when a
new auto-debit mandate is set up - a small nominal amount, with the note flagging
it as a mandate - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being
recognized as a verification entry. And a refund that came back on a card is
landing as a plain refund for some customers when it should read as a card
reversal; a customer on a different type of account sees the same kind of refund
labeled correctly, so the wrong label appears to depend on the account category.

## Scope of impact

Everyday activity - normal purchases, routine transfers, regular deposits - is
categorized and named correctly, which is precisely why this slipped through QA and
why our monitoring dashboards looked healthy. The breakage is confined to a small
set of unusual transaction forms - among them a note or reference that is exactly
a certain number of digits wide - each one hinging on some exact shape of the raw
row rather than anything about the customer, and each form individually uncommon. But they occur right across the customer base, so they
generate a steady trickle of "why is this labeled wrong" tickets and, more
damaging, they poison the spending-category summaries and payee histories that
several downstream features rely on. That combination is why we are treating it
as ship-blocking rather than a backlog item.

## What we need from engineering

The labeling path is fully deterministic and runs offline - hand it the same
transaction and it reproduces the same wrong answer every time - so each of these
is reproducible on demand and can be pinned down exactly. Get the affected forms
labeling and naming correctly again, and do it without disturbing any transaction
that is already labeled right today. A fix that rescues these cases but nudges the
behavior of ordinary, currently-correct transactions is not acceptable: the pass
condition is simply that the specific problem payments described above come out
right and everything else stays exactly where it is.
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the transaction labeling logic.

arguments.prompt:
Explore the /app codebase very thoroughly. I need to find the code responsible for:
1. Categorizing/labeling bank transactions (e.g. CHEQUE, TRANSFER, REFUND, CARD_REVERSAL, MANDATE/verification entries, ACH/NACH salary credits)
2. Extracting the payee/counterparty name from raw statement narration text
3. Any regex patterns matching things like "ACH-BD-NACH-", "GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR", cheque numbers, digit-count-based matching

Report back: exact file paths, function names with line numbers, and a summary of how the categorization pipeline works. Also find all test files related to this. Be very thorough - list every file involved in this pipeline.

# 1. Repository Layout

The repo `/app` contains a single Flask/pandas microservice ("transaction-enrichment-python"). There are **only 50 Python files**, all under `/app/categorizationapp/`. There is **exactly one git commit** (`fc21c7f import codebase`) and **no test files, no CI config, no requirements.txt, no Makefile** (see §6).

```
/app/Dockerfile                                  # gunicorn categorizationapp:app on :9898
/app/.gitignore
/app/categorizationapp/setup.py                  # deps: Flask 1.1.2, pandas 1.2.4, fuzzywuzzy, python-Levenshtein, scipy, sklearn

/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py     # 35 per-bank categorizers
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/*.py  # 13 shared enrichment modules
```

---

# 2. The Categorization Pipeline (how it works)

### Entry points — `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py`
- `home()` — line 52
- `recurrentTransactions()` — line 56 (`POST /recurrentTransactions`)
- **`categorizeTransaction()` — line 70 (`POST /categorizeTransaction`)** ← the main pipeline

`categorizeTransaction()` reads `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `isPFMEnabled`, `transactions[]`, normalizes to a DataFrame (`pd.json_normalize`, line 81), calls `AppUtil.clean_input_df` (line 87), then runs a **giant `if/elif` chain on `bank`** (lines 91–932, one ~24-line copy-pasted block per bank, ending in `else: return "Bank Not Found"` at line 931). Every block executes the identical 6-step sequence:

| Step | Function called | File |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` | `BankScripts/<Bank>.py` |
| 2 | (CREDIT_CARD only) `card_clean_names` → `card_purpose` | `UtilityScripts/CardCleanNames.py`, `CardPurpose.py` |
| 3 | `purpose(transactions, accountType)` | `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` |
| 4 | `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)` | `UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` |
| 5 | `internal_payment(...)` (if accountHolder) | `UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py` |
| 6 | `salary_detection(...)` (SAVING only) → `pfm_categorization` → `simple_description` (if isPFMEnabled) | `SalaryDetection.py`, `PFMCategorization.py`, `SimpleDescription.py` |

### Core mechanic used everywhere
Every module builds a Python list of `[boolean_mask, value]` pairs called `conditions_choices`, wraps it in a DataFrame, then applies `np.select(df['conditions'], df['choices'], default=...)`. **First matching row wins** — so ordering inside these lists is semantically critical. The masks are almost always `transactions.description.str.contains(<regex>, na=False, case=False)` combined with `type.eq("DEBIT"/"CREDIT")`, `amount.lt/gt/eq`, `remark.str.contains`, or `str.count(sep).eq(n)`.

### Output columns produced, in order
1. `transactionCategory` — set in the bank script (default `"TRANSFER"`)
2. `transactionSubcategory` — bank script, then overwritten/refined in `Purpose.py`
3. `merchantType` — bank script + `Purpose.py` (line 278) + `CleanName.py` (line 1956)
4. **`partyName`** — the extracted payee/counterparty (bank script, then normalized in `CleanName.py`)
5. `party2` — `partyName` with all spaces stripped, used for space-insensitive matching
6. `city` (IDBI only), `isInternalPayment`, `Group_ID`, `pfmCategoryOne/Two`, `pfmSimpleDescription`

import sys, json
sys.path.insert(0, '/app/categorizationapp')
import pandas as pd
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts import AppUtil

BANKS = {}
def load():
    from categorizationapp.BankScripts.IDBI import categorize_IDBI_transactions
    from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Indusind import categorize_Indusind_transactions
    from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Axis import categorize_Axis_transactions
    from categorizationapp.BankScripts.HDFC import categorize_HDFC_transactions
    from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Kotak import categorize_Kotak_transactions
    from categorizationapp.BankScripts.BankOfMaharashtra import categorize_BankOfMaharashtra_transactions
    BANKS.update(dict(
        IDBI=categorize_IDBI_transactions,
        INDUSIND=categorize_Indusind_transactions,
        AXIS=categorize_Axis_transactions,
        HDFC=categorize_HDFC_transactions,
        KOTAK=categorize_Kotak_transactions,
        BOM=categorize_BankOfMaharashtra_transactions,
    ))

def run(bank, rows, accountType="SAVING", accountHolder="TEST HOLDER"):
    load()
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    for col, default in [("remark", ""), ("balanceAfterTransaction", 1000.0), ("amount", 100.0),
                         ("type", "DEBIT"), ("description", "")]:
        if col not in df.columns:
            df[col] = default
    df = AppUtil.clean_input_df(df)
    fn = BANKS[bank]
    import inspect
    params = inspect.signature(fn).parameters
    if len(params) == 3:
        out = fn(df, accountType, accountHolder)
    else:
        out = fn(df, accountType)
    return out[["description", "remark", "type", "amount", "transactionCategory", "partyName"]]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    pd.set_option("display.width", 250)
    pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 60)

steps.message:
## Root cause

The regressions were **not spread across the labeling engine** — they were confined to two of the 35 per-bank rule files. Filesystem timestamps made this decisive: every file in the repo carries the original import mtime (`2022-11-02`) except `BankScripts/IDBI.py` and `BankScripts/Indusind.py` (`2026-07-15`). Each reported ticket maps to exactly one rule in those two files, and every fix was cross-validated against the *untouched* sibling banks that implement the identical rule shape.

## The five defects

| Ticket | File:line | Defect | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| Salary shows `NACH` instead of employer | `IDBI.py:83` | `^ACH-BD-NACH` took dash-field `[2:3]` (= `NACH`), making it a duplicate of the next rule for `^ACH-BD-` | `sep_by_dash(...,3,4)` → `ACME INDUSTRIES` (matches untouched `HDFC.py:169`) |
| Sender name blank on `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR` | `IDBI.py:110` | `py_extract(pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)", index=1)` — pattern has only group `0`, so `py_extract` returned an empty Series | `index=0` → `Ravi Kumar` (only such index/group mismatch in the whole codebase) |
| Cheque filed as general transfer | `Indusind.py:64` | Bare-cheque-number remark matched `^[0-9]{5}$` — a fixed width; all 11 sibling banks use a *range*, and line 190 pairs with `[0-9]{5,}` | `^[0-9]{5,6}$` (same as untouched Axis/PNB/BOM) — keeps every currently-tagged 5-digit cheque, restores 6-digit ones |
| Mandate token charge filed as transfer | `Indusind.py:30` | `amount.eq(2)`; nominal verification amount is `1` (or `< 2`) in all 20+ verification rules, and the identical Axis rule uses `eq(1)` | `amount.eq(1)` → `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` |
| Card refund not read as card reversal, depends on account type | `Indusind.py:26` | `accountType=="SAVINGS"` — the app only ever emits `SAVING`, so the rule was dead and the row fell through to the plain `REFUND` rule below it | `"SAVING"` (the only `SAVINGS` occurrence in the repo) |

## Verification

- All five tickets now produce the right category/payee, confirmed through the real `/categorizeTransaction` pipeline (bank script → `purpose` → `clean_names` → PFM).
- A 244-row before/after snapshot over both banks × `SAVING`/`CURRENT` shows **27 changed rows, all of them instances of the five reported forms** — ordinary purchases, transfers, deposits, NEFT/RTGS/IMPS/UPI, charges, ATM and other cheque narrations are byte-identical.
- Boundary sweeps confirm containment: remark widths 1–4 and 7–16, mixed/alphanumeric remarks, `CURRENT`/`OVER_DRAFT`/`CREDIT_CARD` POS credits, `MNDTVRFCHGS` mandate-charge rows and amounts 0.5/1.5/2/3/−1 are all unchanged.
- Total diff: **5 lines across 2 files**; no shared regex constants or utility modules touched.

One note unrelated to this incident: a 3-row Indusind payload with `isPFMEnabled` fails `to_json` in this container — it reproduces identically on the pre-fix file and is caused by the env running pandas 2.2.3 against the pinned 1.2.4.
